Whoaverse is least to say isn't very straightforward to make a working copy out of. Fortunately, I've gotten it to work a while ago and have successfully maintained it with several updates. This is a repost from my comment in this thread, so here goes:

It'll take a while to prepare so be ready. First off, make sure you install Microsoft SQL Server 2012 Express for SQL Server Management and the server itself. After installing those, install Microsoft Visual Studio 2013 for Web

Then finally, use SQL Server Management Studio program you've installed. Connect to your SQL express server and then create 2 empty databases exactly as named: "whoaverse" and "whoaverse_users". Then open the 2 SQL files that you'd find in Git copy of Whoaverse project. Make sure you execute both SQL files and have it successfully execute them correctly.

Now this is kind of an insider bug with Whoaverse, because SQL file wasn't updated. Just browse into SQL databases under "whoaverse" database, under Database Tables, and then right click on "Subverses" table and click on Design Table. Finally, scroll down and click on the first bottom box to create a new column, name it exactly as so: "subscribers" and then click on second box and set it to "int" and make sure "Allow Null" is checked for this row. Press "Control + S" to save the table.

Now, you'll have to create a login for your SQL Connection (it's annoying, but bear with me.) Open up the "Security" directory under your SQL Express Server, then right click on Login directory and click on "New Login." For simplicity sake, just make log in name to "whoaverse" and click on SQL Server Authenication and set the password to "secretpwd" or whatever you prefer and then uncheck Enforce Password Policy (You're doing it on the LAN, so it's fine for development purpose.) Set the default database to "whoaverse" database and click on "Server Roles" and check all the things. Click on User Mapping, check all the things for your 2 whoaverse databases. Click ok and that it. Now you have to enable the TCP communication for your SQL Express Server. Right click your SQL Express Server and then click on Properties, then click on Connections in the new window and then click on Allow Remote Connection to this Server and click ok. Then finally, restart your server by right clicking on the server again and then click on Restart button, new dialog would show up asking you if you really want to do it, then you have to click ok on that as well.

You now have a working database, now browse into Whoaverse project folder and right click on "Whoaverse.sln" file and Open With Visual Studio 2013 for Web program. You're almost done with the whole crapload of work. Now right click on Whoaverse project in your solution explorer window and click on "Add Existing Item" and go to parent directories until you find "Web.config" file and go ahead and add that. Now open up your Web.config file, and copy from my Config file which is already made for login "whoaverse" and password "secretpwd". If your login isn't those, then you'll need to look through that config file carefully and edit for 2 connection strings:

Look for this phrase in your connection string: "User ID=whoaverse;Password=secretpwd"

If you've got it all in, then finally, click on the green arrow button in your Visual Studio to run the project and view it in your favorite web browser (I pray it isn't IE...) and if all goes well, you have a working copy, if not, please do tell me what went wrong. I hope this helps.

So I hope this would allow you to try getting your hands dirty with Whoaverse and see if you could solve some of the problem it has.
Instruction to how to set up a working copy of Whoaverse
